text:
maya: Heads up - provisioning in ap-south1 is stalling, seeing lots of tiny pending GPU pods and slow node creation.

sam: noticed that too, kube events show repeated taint application and then immediate preempt evictions.

lee: stacktrace from the scheduler logs looks like binpack score thrashing when mix of fractional-gang and strict-affinity pods land. quick snippet:```I0312 14:02:10.123456 1 scheduler.go:234] scoring node node-az1 Rack=R3 score=6.2
I0312 14:02:10.123789 1 scheduler.go:237] selected node node-az2 score=6.2```

maya: also seeing VPC egress quotas being hit for the provisioner; AMI pulls and init scripts slowed to 20-30s each which magnifies fragmentation.

olivia: @maya can you paste the `kubectl get events` for one of the pending pods? curious if it's image pull or admission.

maya: here you go - short:```Normal Pulling 2m (x3) kubelet pulling image "company/base-gpu:latest"
Warning Failed 2m (x3) kubelet failed to start container: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = network egress quota exceeded```

sam: that explains long init times. nodes come up slower -> scheduler packs small pods onto new nodes because of early scoring -> creates fragmentation pockets.

diego: cost note: we've been autoscaling new G4 pools in ap-south1 on demand. slow init + tiny pod spread => we spin many racks with 1-2 GPUs used. that's a 3x unit cost increase for that workload.

lee: quick mitigation idea: temporarily bias scheduler scoring to favor node fill (reduce spread) for ap-south1 until egress quotas caught up. can we gate that by label? e.g., apply `node.kubernetes.io/egress-throttled=true` and change scoring weights.

olivia: we could also throttle the provisioner to create nodes in bursts of 4 instead of 1, to reduce the number of half-empty racks. challenging with current autoscaler config tho.

maya: infra-bot reported recent change to VPC NAT scaling at 14:00 - appears rollout to ap-south1 didn't apply the new SNAT table correctly. infra-bot: "deploy/nat-gateway-controller v2.1 rolled out to ap-south1 (3/4 nodes applied)"

scheduler-service: FYI I can expose an override flag `/config/binpack_bias=0.8` to favor binpack over spread for a limited period. Requires config rollout and restart of scheduler (rolling, non-disruptive).

sam: low-risk plan: 1) set scheduler binpack_bias to 0.8 for ap-south1 2) mark new nodes with egress-throttled label 3) trigger orchestrator to provision nodes in bursts of 4 4) monitor pod pending time and cost metric `gpu.utilization/row` for 1h

diego: +1 on plan, but add budget guard: if cost/instance > 1.8x baseline alert and revert.

olivia: I'll take NAT rollout fix, initiating full apply to the remaining SNAT nodes now. ETA 12m.

maya: applying scheduler override now in canary to two schedulers in ap-south1. watching.

(small pause)

maya: canary looks promising, pending pods cleared from 320 -> 18 in 90s. startup latencies decreased.

sam: cost signal still spiky, but trending down. leaving binpack override for next 45m then re-evaluate.

diego: filing a follow-up ticket to rethink autoscaler burst policy and image caching in init images to avoid VPC egress dependency. linking in infra-runbook.

olivia: NAT apply complete. keeping watch on SNAT metrics. if we continue to see egress saturation we'll route image pulls to internal registry mirror.

lee: nice. next steps: schedule a short retro tomorrow to decide if this becomes an autoscaler policy change or a scheduler feature (per-zone binpack bias).

maya: thanks all, will post brief summary in incidents channel after we confirm stable. :thumbsup:
